problems.name: See the words, priority and money together
problems.summary: A reader can say, without scrolling or reading a paragraph, what the official said, what the donor says it wants and what was given, and which words the two share.

problems.name: Show doubt and caveats without implying cause
problems.summary: A reader sees the speaker-credit doubt, which words are shared and that the card is a reading, and cannot take the card as saying the money caused the words.

problems.name: Show money without inviting a sum
problems.summary: A reader sees what was given through each committee and any outside spending and is never offered, or led toward, a total across committees or outside spending.

problems.name: Serve scanning, reading and checking
problems.summary: A reader scanning many cards, one reading a card closely and one checking its sources each get what they need without the others' clutter.

dimensions.problem: See the words, priority and money together
dimensions.name: How the card is laid out

options.name: Three zones side by side
options.description: Money then the donor's priority on the left, the official in the middle, the official's exact words on the right; stacked in that order on a phone (mockup option A).

options.name: Words first
options.description: The official's name and exact words are the headline; the donor's priority and the money sit under them, side by side on a computer, stacked on a phone (mockup option B).

options.name: Matched pair with a money ledger
options.description: The words and the donor's priority face each other in two columns with the shared words listed between them; the money is a ledger in its own box beneath (mockup option C).

options.name: Glance row that opens
options.description: In a list each card is a short row: names, shared words, the first words cut at a word boundary with the cut marked, one line per committee, the doubt badge and a flag when outside spending exists; the whole card opens in place or on its own page (mockup option D).

dimensions.why_it_matters: The layout decides which of the three a reader meets first and whether the shared words are seen across two texts or inside one; it is worth seeing built more than one way because it is judged by readers, not by the data.

dimensions.problem: See the words, priority and money together
dimensions.name: What a phone does with the zones

options.name: Stack in zone order
options.description: On a phone the zones stack as on a computer: money, donor priority, official, words.

options.name: Words first on a phone
options.description: On a phone the words and the official come first, then the priority, then the money.

options.name: Fold zones behind headings
options.description: On a phone each zone is a heading that opens (money, donor's priority, words), with the shared words and the doubt badge always visible above them.

dimensions.why_it_matters: Most of the layouts above are really three phone orderings; choosing the order is choosing what a thumb meets first.

dimensions.problem: Show doubt and caveats without implying cause
dimensions.name: Where the reading strip sits

options.name: Under the three zones
options.description: The strip is a full-width dashed band between the zones and the sources row, labelled 'Reading, not a finding.'

options.name: Between the words and the money
options.description: The strip sits between the words-and-priority block and the money block, so the two are never read side by side without it.

options.name: As a label at the top
options.description: The card opens with a one-line label, the doubt badge and 'Reading, not a finding. No cause is claimed.'; the in-common and differs sentences stay under the zones.

dimensions.why_it_matters: The strip is the card's only statement of what the pairing is; where it sits decides whether a reader meets it before or after the money.

dimensions.problem: Show doubt and caveats without implying cause
dimensions.name: How speaker-credit doubt is shown

options.name: Badge with the level only
options.description: A coloured badge reads 'SPEAKER-CREDIT DOUBT: HIGH' and nothing more.

options.name: Badge with the reason on the card
options.description: The badge and the reason sentences sit together in the reading strip (as mocked in A to D).

options.name: Badge that opens its reason
options.description: The badge is a control that opens the reason beside it; in a list only the badge shows.

dimensions.why_it_matters: The doubt is about whether the words are the official's at all; on card 4 (high) the caption names the speaker only phonetically.

dimensions.problem: Show doubt and caveats without implying cause
dimensions.name: How shared words are marked

options.name: Highlight in both texts
options.description: The shared words are wrapped in a highlight in the official's words and in the donor's bubble (mocked in A to D).

options.name: Shared-word chips
options.description: The shared words are also listed as chips between or above the texts (mocked in C and D).

options.name: A plain line when nothing is shared
options.description: A card with no literally shared words says 'none of substance, so nothing is highlighted' and shows no chips.

dimensions.why_it_matters: Highlights are the card's strongest visual claim of a link, so how far they reach decides how much a reader thinks the two texts agree.

dimensions.problem: Show money without inviting a sum
dimensions.name: How committee lines are laid out

options.name: One block per committee
options.description: Each committee is its own block with its total as the largest text, labelled 'Schedule A, this committee only', and a note after the last: none is added to another (mocked in A, B, D).

options.name: A ledger table
options.description: A table with one row per committee and columns for total, committee, kind, rows and dates, and giver as filed (mocked in C).

options.name: One compact line per committee in lists
options.description: In a list each committee is one line, amount first, with 'this committee only' and the committee name; kind, rows and dates are on the card (mocked in D).

dimensions.why_it_matters: Three of the five built cards (3, 4 and 5) have two committees each, and the Mayor's two cards have one measure committee each (the funding map lists three ballot-measure committees carrying his name, one terminated and without a card), so what a second line looks like decides whether a total is invited.

dimensions.problem: Show money without inviting a sum
dimensions.name: How outside spending is kept apart

options.name: A separate dashed box below the gifts
options.description: Outside spending is a box with a different border and colour, headed 'Outside spending, kept apart', saying it is not a gift to any committee above and not added to one; each report line stands alone (mocked in A to C).

options.name: A flag in the list and a box on the card
options.description: In a list the row carries a flag, 'Outside spending, kept apart: open the card', and no amount; the box is on the card (mocked in D).

options.name: Left off the card and linked
options.description: The card shows gifts only, with a line saying outside spending also exists and linking to the funding map section that lists it.

dimensions.why_it_matters: The earlier worked pairings found outside spending, not gifts, for the one donor with money, so a card must show it without its reading as a gift.

dimensions.problem: Show money without inviting a sum
dimensions.name: How a many-to-one donor is shown

options.name: One bubble with a tie note
options.description: One donor bubble, with an italic line saying how the tie is recognised, by Filers id or by name only (mocked in every option).

options.name: Giver names as a count that opens
options.description: The money line shows '15 giver names as filed' and the count opens to the full list in place (mocked in A to D when a line has more than three names).

options.name: Giver names listed as filed
options.description: Every giver name is listed in the money line.

dimensions.why_it_matters: A bubble that holds many names must say how each is tied, or a reader takes a name match for a fact.

dimensions.name: What the list shows of each card

options.name: The whole card
options.description: Every card in the list is the whole card (mocked in A to C).

options.name: A row that opens
options.description: Each card is a row of names, shared words, cut words, one line per committee and the badge; it opens in place to the whole card (mocked in D).

options.name: The words cut with the card a click away
options.description: Each card shows only the official and the words (cut if long) and the doubt badge; money and priority are on the card's page.

dimensions.why_it_matters: The list is how most readers meet the cards, so what it omits is what most readers never see.

dimensions.name: What the card's own page adds

options.name: Row-level filing table
options.description: Under each committee line, a table of each Schedule A row with date, filing id and version, filing date, amount and giver as filed, with 24-hour repeats listed apart (the built site's card already does this).

options.name: Recording and transcript links
options.description: The words carry a link to the city transcript at its time stamp and, where there is one, to the meeting recording.

options.name: A copyable link and a printable view
options.description: The page has its own address that can be copied, and prints as a single card without navigation.

dimensions.why_it_matters: The page is where a reporter verifies a pairing, so what it adds sets how long verification takes.

dimensions.name: Where sources sit

options.name: One sources row at the bottom
options.description: A single row at the bottom links the transcript, the donor page and the filing ids and gives the money retrieval date (as the maintainer described, mocked in A to D).

options.name: A source link beside each element
options.description: Each part carries its own link: the words a transcript link, the priority a source link, the money its dataset link (the mockups include the first two in the words and the priority and keep the row).

options.name: Both
options.description: Links beside each element and a sources row that collects them with the retrieval date.

dimensions.why_it_matters: Sources are what makes a card checkable, and a source far from the claim it supports is slower to check.
